stratified_split.source:
def _split(
    by_tool: dict[str, list[TrainExample]], frac: float, rng: rand.Generator
) -> tuple[list[TrainExample], list[TrainExample]]:
    """Per-tool stratified split so every trained tool keeps eval coverage.

    A tool with ≥2 examples always contributes ≥1 eval (and keeps ≥1 train);
    a singleton goes entirely to train (nothing to hold out).
    """
    train: list[TrainExample] = []
    ev: list[TrainExample] = []
    for exs in by_tool.values():
        shuffled = exs[:]
        rng.shuffle(shuffled)
        n = len(shuffled)
        n_eval = 0 if n < 2 else min(n - 1, max(1, round(n * frac)))
        ev.extend(shuffled[:n_eval])
        train.extend(shuffled[n_eval:])
    return train, ev
